title: Mouse Model Protocol for Bilateral Maxillary First Molar Extraction and Alveolar Bone Healing Study
author: Jiang, Mou, et al.
materials: disposable syringe needles (23G, 25 mm; and 26G, 15 mm)

Timing: 10 min (not including autoclave time)
1.Prepare and sterilize the following instruments and materials to ensure aseptic surgical condition is maintained:a.A new set of disposable syringe needles (23G, 25 mm; and 26G, 15 mm) for each mouse to serve as dental elevators (Figure 1A).Figure 1Surgical Preparation(A) Instruments for tooth extraction: 23G and 26G syringe needles (used as dental elevators), blunt-tipped tissue forceps (used as buccal retractors), and toothed ophthalmic micro-forceps(used for tooth grasping and luxation).(B) Magnified view of the toothed tips of the ophthalmic micro-forceps.(C) Complete surgical instrument and supply setup.(D) Preparation of the mouse tracheal intubation platform.b.Tissue forceps with blunt, rounded tips to serve as buccal retractors during exposure of the maxillary molar region (Figure 1A).c.Ophthalmic micro-forceps with serrated (toothed) tips to grasp and extract the maxillary first molar.1 (Figures 1A and 1B).d.Sterile surgical drapes to cover surgical table and mouse tracheal intubation platform.e.Two rubber bands to depress and stabilize the mandible, serving as an adjustable mouth opener (Figure 1C).f.Sterile cotton balls, torn into small pieces (approximately 3–5mm diameter) to be used for hemostasis and cleaning the surgical site (Figure 1C).g.Sterile gauze pads to support the neck and protect the cervical spine during surgery (Figure 1C).h.Small surgical scissors to incise the oral commissures and dissect soft tissues from the maxilla during sample preparation (Figure 1C).
Note: Sterilize all surgical instruments and materials using a gravity autoclave cycle at 121°C for 15 min,5 or according to the sterilization-pouch manufacturer’s instructions. As rubber bands cannot be autoclaved due to heat sensitivity, disinfect them by immersing in 70% ethanol for at least 15 min.5 After disinfection, rinse the rubber bands thoroughly with sterile saline or sterile water and allow them to air-dry under aseptic conditions before use.6
Alternatives: Rubber bands can also be prepared by cutting thin elastic strips from a medical-grade latex glove,1 which provides an accessible, sterile-compatible substitute when commercial rubber bands are unavailable.
2.Prepare and disinfect the following equipment:a.Mouse tracheal intubation platform (20 × 15 × 4.5 cm) with adjustable angulation from 0° to 90° for optimal positioning of the mouse during surgery (Figure 1C).b.Feedback-controlled heating pad (18 × 10 cm) to maintain the mouse’s body temperature during surgery.c.Connect the stereomicroscope to a power supply and ensure adequate illumination for clear visualization during surgery.
Note: Thoroughly disinfect these equipment with 75% ethanol.
Alternatives: Dental loupes (typically 3.5×–4.5× magnification) serve as an effective alternative to the stereomicroscope and provide sufficient visualization for the extraction procedure.7,8

steps.title: Sterilize Instruments and Materials
steps.instruction: Sterilize all surgical instruments (23G 25 mm and 26G 15 mm disposable syringe needles, blunt‑tipped tissue forceps, toothed ophthalmic micro‑forceps, small surgical scissors) and supplies (sterile surgical drapes, two rubber bands, sterile cotton balls ~3–5 mm, sterile gauze pads) using a gravity autoclave cycle at 121 °C for 15 min (or per manufacturer). Because rubber bands cannot be autoclaved, immerse them in 70 % ethanol for at least 15 min, rinse thoroughly with sterile saline or sterile water, and air‑dry under aseptic conditions. As an alternative, thin elastic strips cut from a medical‑grade latex glove may be used as rubber‑band substitutes.

steps.title: Disinfect Equipment
steps.instruction: Wipe the mouse tracheal intubation platform (20 × 15 × 4.5 cm, adjustable 0°–90°), the feedback‑controlled heating pad (18 × 10 cm), and the stereomicroscope (or its power supply and illumination) with 75 % ethanol and allow to dry.

steps.title: Prepare Surgical Workspace
steps.instruction: Clear the surgical table of unnecessary items and disinfect it with 75 % ethanol. Don a clean gown, head cover, surgical mask, and sterile gloves. Cover the table with a sterile drape to create a sterile field. Open the sterilized instruments and arrange them neatly on the drape. Place the mouse tracheal intubation platform on the table and set its angle to approximately 45°–60°. Position the heating pad over the platform, plug it in, and turn it on; then cover the pad with a sterile drape. Lay the two sterile rubber bands on the draped platform for later use as mouth retractors. Position a sterile gauze pad beneath the stainless‑steel wire on the platform to support the mouse’s neck and protect the cervical spine.

steps.title: Induce General Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Disinfect the abdominal injection site with povidone‑iodine. Inject 1 % pentobarbital sodium intraperitoneally at 50 mg/kg. Verify adequate anesthesia by performing a toe‑ or tail‑pinch reflex test; if a reflex persists, wait several minutes and retest. (Alternative approved regimens: ketamine 100 mg/kg + xylazine 5–10 mg/kg i.p.; supplement with one‑third of the initial ketamine dose only, no additional xylazine.) Continuously monitor depth of anesthesia throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Protect Eyes
steps.instruction: Hold the anesthetized mouse in a supine position. Apply ophthalmic ointment onto two sterile cotton balls (≈3–5 mm) and place the ointment‑coated balls over the mouse’s eyes to prevent dryness and light exposure.

steps.title: Administer Pre‑operative Analgesia
steps.instruction: Disinfect the dorsal neck injection site with povidone‑iodine. Inject Carprofen subcutaneously at 5.0 mg/kg immediately before tooth extraction.

steps.title: Extract Right Maxillary First Molar
steps.instruction: Using toothed ophthalmic micro‑forceps, grasp the entire crown of the right maxillary first molar with the serrated tips oriented toward the buccal root and extend the tips beneath the furcation to engage the tooth. Slightly oscillate the forceps buccally and palatally while applying outward traction to increase mobility. Slowly luxate and extract the tooth in the buccal direction with controlled force, avoiding rotational force; the extraction typically requires 1–3 min. Place sterile dry cotton balls or a small piece of sterile gauze into the socket to achieve hemostasis. Examine the extracted tooth under a stereomicroscope to confirm that all three roots (mesial, distal, palatal) are intact, that no root fracture or bone fragment remains attached. Inspect the socket for residual root fragments and assess the interalveolar septum for fracture.

steps.title: Extract Left Maxillary First Molar
steps.instruction: Repeat the procedure described in the previous step on the left maxillary first molar.

description: This protocol establishes a reproducible mouse model of extraction socket healing, suitable for downstream genomic, histological, and micro-CT analyses at defined time points (e.g., immediately after extraction, or at 7, 14, and 21 days post-surgery), as well as for investigating the use of regenerative biomaterials in models of alveolar ridge preservation.
